source.author: cic
source.text: Quod vero in extrema oratione quasi tuo iure sumpsisti, oratorem in omnis sermonis disputatione copiosissime versari posse, id, nisi hic in tuo regno essemus, non tulissem multisque praeessem, qui aut interdicto tecum contenderent aut te ex iure manum consertum vocarent, quod in alienas possessiones tam temere irruisses.
source.text_original: Quod vero in extrema oratione quasi tuo iure sumpsisti, oratorem in omnis sermonis disputatione copiosissime versari posse, id, nisi hic in tuo regno essemus, non tulissem multisque praeessem, qui aut interdicto tecum contenderent aut te ex iure manum consertum vocarent, quod in alienas possessiones tam temere irruisses.
source.text_english: But as to what you took in your closing speech, as if by your own right, namely that an orator can deal most fully with every kind of discussion and conversation, I should not have allowed that, unless we were here in your own kingdom, and I should have been setting over many men who would contend with you either by an interdict or would summon you to join issue on a claim in due form of law, because you had so rashly broken into another man’s possessions.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: in quodcumque uitium stili mei mucro contorquetur, te clamitas designari, conserta manu in ius uocas et satiricum scriptorem in prosa stulte arguis.
reuse.text_original: in quodcumque uitium stili mei mucro contorquetur, te clamitas designari, conserta manu in ius uocas et satiricum scriptorem in prosa stulte arguis.
reuse.text_english: Whatever fault the point of my style is twisted against, you shout that you are being targeted, and, with clenched fist, you summon me to court, and foolishly accuse the satiric writer in prose.
